items: Explain VPC, subnet, security group, and NACL and how they isolate resources.
Apply the principle of least privilege with IAM.
Describe Zero Trust as a security model.
Reason about network and identity boundaries when designing a cloud solution.
VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) — an isolated virtual network you define in the cloud.
Subnet — a segmented range of IP addresses within a VPC (public vs. private).
Security Group — a stateful, instance/resource-level firewall (allow rules).
NACL (Network ACL) — a stateless, subnet-level firewall (allow/deny rules).
IAM (Identity & Access Management) — controls who/what can do what (least privilege).
Zero Trust — never trust, always verify; no implicit trust by network location.

blocks.text: A VPC is your own logically isolated section of the cloud. Inside it you create subnets — typically public subnets (with a route to the internet) for load balancers and bastion hosts, and private subnets for application and data tiers that should not be directly reachable. Segmentation limits blast radius: a compromise in one subnet should not expose everything.

Security Groups are stateful and attached to a resource (e.g., a VM or service). If you allow inbound traffic, the response is automatically allowed back out. They act as the primary allow-list. NACLs are stateless and operate at the subnet boundary; each direction must be explicitly ruled, and rules are evaluated in order. Use NACLs as a coarse subnet-level guard and security groups for fine-grained resource control.
Identity with IAM and least privilege

IAM governs identities (users, roles, services) and their permissions. The least privilege principle grants only the permissions required for a task — nothing more. Prefer roles over long-lived keys, scope policies tightly, and separate human and machine identities.

Zero Trust abandons the old "inside the network = trusted" assumption. Every request is authenticated, authorized, and encrypted regardless of origin. It combines strong identity (IAM), micro-segmentation (VPC/subnets), and continuous verification. For an SA, Zero Trust means designing systems that do not implicitly trust network location.
